chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them both) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi and Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Yazid al-Anbari the scribe narrated to us from Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves us, the Ahl al-Bayt, should praise God for the first of blessings.
It was said: What is the first of blessings? He said: A pure birth. And none loves us except one whose birth is pure.

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahl al-Bayt — the Prophet's household, specifically the Imams and Fatima al-Zahra; the central object of devotion in Shia theology
key_terms.النعم: Divine blessings/favors — here referring to the spiritual prerequisites that enable genuine love of the Imams
key_terms.طيب الولادة: Purity of birth — being born of lawful/honorable parentage, free from the taint of illicit union

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about loving the Ahl al-Bayt and pure birth?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) declares that genuine love for the Ahl al-Bayt is a divine gift requiring gratitude, rooted in the fundamental blessing of pure birth and honorable lineage. In early Islamic thought, 'purity of birth' (tayyib al-wilada) meant being born of lawful parents outside of pre-Islamic forbidden unions — reflecting the belief that authentic love of the Prophet's family is both spiritually innate and morally conditioned. This teaching, transmitted through a long chain from Imam al-Sadiq back to the Prophet, underscores the Shia theological position that attachment to the Ahl al-Bayt is a mark of divine favor and spiritual soundness.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan (ra) narrated to us. They said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid. He said: Abu'l Qasim `Abd al-Rahman al-Kufi and Abu Yusuf Ya`qub al-Anbari the scribe narrated to us from Abi Muhammad `Abdullah b. Muhammad al-Ghifari from al-Husayn b. Zayd from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Whoever loves us, the Ahl al-Bayt, should praise Allah for the first of blessings.
It was said: What is the first of blessings? He said: A pure birth. None loves us except he whose birth is pure.
